newsitem.title: FINLAND: Yeltsin says he and Clinton face difficult talks.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says he and Clinton face difficult talks.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, arriving in Finland for a summit with the U.S. president, said on Thursday the two leaders faced difficult talks but would try to find compromises and part as friends.

"President Bill Clinton and I face difficult, serious talks," he told reporters. "But the main thing we have to remember is that not only our countries are following our decisions. Europe and the whole world are also watching so that we do not lose the partnership which has been developed in recent years."
Yeltsin, speaking after arriving at Helsinki's Vantaa airport aboard his new Ilyushin-96 presidential jet, looked fit and walked down the steps to the tarmac accompanied by his wife Naina.

"I think Bill Clinton and his team are of a mind to find constructive approaches and find compromises so that we can agree on all aspects of disputed questions and part as we have after other such meetings -- as friends," he said.

Yeltsin's remarks, while promising a tough fight at the two-day summit, suggested he wanted to avoid lasting damage to the relationship with Washington, seen as a crucial partner as Russia struggles to develop its market economy.
Clinton arrived earlier and the two men meet later for their first summit session over dinner.
